units.name: Protocol
units.necessity: Fixes what counts as the topic before any result is seen (PRISMA-ScR), so later screening cannot drift toward convenient papers.
units.trigger: First Unit of a topic: a topic file exists and step0 has no protocol, or the topic file's hash changed (P10 STALE).
preconditions: the topic file exists and is readable
no Unit of the topic is running
logic: choose the question framework by the question's semantics (PICO, PECO, PCC, SPIDER, ... or custom), never force-filled
give every slot a value, an operational role and a searchability reason
write 2-4 search axes as OR-clusters of 1-4 word terms without operators
list outcomes and >= 1 inclusion and >= 1 exclusion criterion, each outcome cited by a criterion
write the timeframe with its reason and the completion criterion
submit the draft through frame set-protocol, which validates (P01-P11) and computes topic_sha256 / history
units.state: Instance per topic. The draft lives in _state/A1/protocol.json (scratch); the tool owns the step0 keys. Later changes go through frame set-protocol --note or A2.c's declared revisions (add/retire terms) and are logged in protocol.history.

error_boundary.local_recovery: a draft that fails P01-P11 is corrected by the model and re-submitted; the tool never writes a failing protocol
error_boundary.escalation: framework misfit is caught downstream by A1.e (LOOP-02)

units.idempotency: Re-submitting the same draft rewrites identical keys; a changed draft appends to history and makes A1.q, A1.e and everything downstream stale.
units.security: No network. Reads the topic file and the files it names only; writes only its step0 keys through the tool (atomic temp-file + rename).

verdict.problem: Without a pre-registered frame the search and screening criteria are written after seeing results.
verdict.why_separate: It is the only Unit that decides scope; A1.q translates it into queries and A1.e judges it independently.
verdict.if_removed: Queries and criteria would be invented ad hoc; A1.e and A3 would have nothing fixed to check against.
verdict.merge: Merging with A1.q was the original single-step design (research-init); it hid scope decisions inside query wording.
verdict.boundary: Well-defined: owns five step0 keys; schema ideate-protocol/1.
verdict.quality: Judgement fields are separated from computed fields; P01-P11 each have a counter-example; L4.
verdict.alternatives: PICO-only frame (rejected: forces slots that do not fit non-clinical topics).
verdict.risks: A wrong frame propagates to every Unit (mitigated by A1.e).

units.name: Query strategy
units.necessity: Turns the protocol's axes into query variants each database can parse, plus anchors and known items that later test the search.
units.trigger: A1.p done; or A2.c revises a query (LOOP-01).

side_effects: scope probe network calls (read-only, recorded under _state/probes/A1q/)

preconditions: A1.p done and its checks pass
logic: compose each query as a combination of axes (Boolean form rendered by the tool, flat form of 3-5 content words)
add the variants the depth needs (quick 3, standard 5, deep 7)
name 2-5 anchor terms, >= 2 sources, and >= 2 known items from standard depth
submit through frame set-strategy (Q01-Q22)
run the scope probe (standard, deep) and record yields per source
units.state: Instance per topic; later changes are A2.c revisions, not new instances. strategy_basis pins the protocol hash it was built on (Q21); scope_probe pins the strategy hash (Q20).

error_boundary.local_recovery: probe failure records scope_probe.skipped (caveat probe-skipped) and the search still runs
error_boundary.escalation: hard stop when A1.p has errors

units.idempotency: set-strategy with unchanged queries keeps the probe; changed queries drop it and make A2.s instances of those queries stale.
units.security: Outbound read-only probe to the scholar server and OpenAlex; keys from the environment; probe answers stored without credentials.

verdict.problem: Backends AND every word of a long query (0 hits, slide 2) and each parses a different syntax.
verdict.why_separate: Query wording is revised after the search (LOOP-01) without touching the protocol.
verdict.if_removed: A2.s would need to invent queries; A2.c could not revise them through a declared interface.
verdict.merge: Could merge with A1.p, but then every query revision would invalidate the protocol evaluation.
verdict.boundary: Owns eight step0 keys; schemas declared on the card.
verdict.cost_risk: About 5 min + probe 1-2 min; probe adds network dependence (degradable).
verdict.quality: Rendered fields recomputed (Q18 catches hand edits); L4.
verdict.alternatives: One flat query per outcome (legacy flow, slide 2) - lost recall.
verdict.benefits: Replayable, per-source renderings; known items give a recall test.
verdict.risks: Known items may be invented (caught when no database has them).

units.name: Protocol evaluation
units.necessity: An independent reader judges the protocol and strategy before any search (Kitchenham), which the author model cannot do for itself.
units.trigger: A1.p and A1.q done; again after the one forced revision (LOOP-02).

context: nothing else: the brief names only these two paths

commands: (one subagent reads the brief and returns JSON)
preconditions: A1.p and A1.q have no errors (the brief is refused otherwise)
logic: render a brief that names only the topic file and step1_protocol.md
a fresh subagent returns findings E1-E6 with evidence and a verdict
set-evaluation checks the findings against the verdict (E01-E06)
revision-required in round 1 -> one forced revision of A1.p/A1.q, then round 2
round 2 still revision-required -> final status accepted-with-doubts (caveat protocol-doubts, must disclose)
units.state: Rounds 1-2 stored in step1_protocol_evaluation.json with the protocol hash they judged; a brief without its stored round means 'ask the reader again'.

error_boundary.local_recovery: malformed JSON is fixed once, then the reader is asked again (RP-MODEL-OUTPUT inside a round)
error_boundary.escalation: accepted-with-doubts travels as a must-disclose caveat into the idea's Risk Factors

units.idempotency: Per round: re-asking a round whose answer is stored is refused; a new round needs a changed protocol.
units.security: Subagent sees no network, no research folder beyond the two paths, and not the main session's reasoning (isolation is the purpose).

verdict.problem: Self-review by the protocol's author is not independent.
verdict.why_separate: Isolation (two input paths only) is the design; merging would break it.
verdict.if_removed: The frame would go unchecked into a 1-2 M token screening run.
verdict.boundary: Inputs restricted by the brief; output schema ideate-protocol-eval/1.
verdict.cost_risk: One subagent, ~3 min, 30-60k tokens per round; bounded to 2 rounds.
verdict.alternatives: Human checkpoint 1 of the original engine (removed by decision D-09).
verdict.evidence: slide 3 A1.e: forced revision once, then accepted-with-doubts.
verdict.risks: A lenient reader; mitigated by E06 (criterion readings).

units.name: Context
units.necessity: Records who the work is for (target venues, expert domain) and what this machine has, for the lens (B1) and the journal step (B6.3).
units.trigger: Any time after A1.p and before B1; the legacy `next` offers it right after A1.e.
units.legacy_deviation: The legacy registry files A1.v under block 'planning' although slide 3 places it in step Define; v2 places it in STEP-S1.

context: data roots the topic file names

logic: name 2-4 target venues and the expert domain
list artefacts, cached data, packages present and missing
submit through frame set-context (V01)
units.state: Instance per topic; may be re-run at any time; never touches local_environment.probe (B1's).

error_boundary.local_recovery: an empty environment is a valid answer (the lists say the machine was looked at)

units.idempotency: Re-running rewrites its keys; affects only later generations' B2/B6.3.
units.security: No network; local import checks only.

verdict.problem: Stage B needs venues and domain; the lens needs the local context.
verdict.why_separate: Independent of the search (no search Unit reads it) and cheap to redo.
verdict.if_removed: B1 would lack the persona inputs and B6.3 would have no venue targets.
verdict.merge: Could merge into B1 (lens) since only Stage B reads it; kept separate because the slide puts it in Define and it is written once per topic.
verdict.duplication: Overlaps B1's env-probe in the 'local environment' prose; B1's probe is authoritative for gates.
verdict.boundary: Output well-defined, but its dependency edge is undeclared: no Unit requires A1.v and no gate checks it (validator C-IO-ORDER).
verdict.dependencies: None declared; implicitly upstream of B1 and B6.
verdict.alternatives: Move into B1 (rejected for now: slide 3 places it in S1).
verdict.evidence: ideate_units.json A1.v block=planning; it_ledger.next_unit special-cases A1.v.
verdict.benefits: Making the edge explicit guarantees B1/B6 read written context.
verdict.risks: Changing B1.requires makes B1 stale on existing topics until A1.v is recorded done.
verdict.actions: Adopt D-12 (B1 requires A1.v) or add A1.v to GATE-align-check; fix the registry block label.

units.name: Retrieval
units.necessity: Runs every query against every chosen source in the form that source parses, and records every attempt so the search is replayable (PRISMA-S).
units.trigger: GATE-frame-check passed; or a query's rendering changed (new instance).

side_effects: network requests to the scholar sources, recorded under _state/net/

logic: for each active query: render per source (Boolean, Boolean without stars, arXiv, flat)
request the top 50 by relevance per source; record sent string, time, filters, returned/total or error
run the dense instance D1 from resolved known items (standard, deep)
a source failing on two queries running is benched, retried once after a wait
units.state: One instance file per (query id, rendering hash); 'complete' set only when every planned source answered, errored or was skipped; incremental resume re-runs only incomplete instances.

error_boundary.local_recovery: bench-and-retry per source; still failing -> caveat source-failed; no answer from a source at all -> source-dead (must disclose); D1 skipped -> dense-skipped
error_boundary.escalation: hard stop when every query failed on every source

units.idempotency: Instance identity = query id + rendering hash; a complete instance is never re-run unless --force; replay mode (IDEATE_REPLAY=1) re-runs offline.
units.security: Outbound HTTPS to PubMed, Scopus, IEEE, WoS, OpenAlex, arXiv, Semantic Scholar; keys from env/.env, never printed; recordings exclude credentials.

verdict.problem: Database search is the only network-heavy, non-judgement step of the search.
verdict.why_separate: Pure mechanics with its own failure modes (rate limits, keys); A2.m and A2.c must not depend on network timing.
verdict.merge: Merging with A2.m would couple per-query resume to whole-collection merging.
verdict.boundary: One file per instance, schema ideate-query-instance/1.
verdict.dependencies: A1.e is a deliberate gate (no search on an unevaluated protocol).
verdict.cost_risk: 30-60 s per query plus waits; no tokens; S2 rate limits observed on every query in the 2026-10-17 run.
verdict.quality: Deterministic given recordings; replay and interrupt tests; L4.
verdict.alternatives: LLM-driven search calls (original engine) - not replayable.
verdict.evidence: slide 3 A2.s; run 2026-10-17: 933 papers, S2 throttled on every query.
verdict.risks: scholar_mcp's pacing uses POSIX fcntl and fails on Windows (OQ-08).

units.name: Merge
units.necessity: Turns many query instances into one deduplicated collection with stable, never-reused ids and PRISMA identification counts.

side_effects: DOI recovery (scholar) and batched OpenAlex enrichment, recorded

logic: merge by DOI, then arXiv id, then fuzzy/exact title; keep found_by
assign ids append-only (an id is never reused; a re-run query's old-instance papers are kept)
enrich in OpenAlex batches; compute SPECTER2 sem_sim / sem_pct
write identification counts and the search summary
units.state: _state/paper_ids.jsonl is append-only and shared by part with A5 (minted_by).

error_boundary.local_recovery: enrichment batch failure leaves abstracts missing (degraded); no S2 key -> doi-recovery-skipped; no SPECTER2 -> no sem_sim
error_boundary.escalation: hard stop when there is no instance to merge

units.idempotency: Deterministic on unchanged instances and recordings: rerun produces identical output, so nothing downstream goes stale.
units.security: Outbound to the scholar server and OpenAlex; no credentials stored.

verdict.problem: Stable ids and dedup are what every later file is keyed on.
verdict.why_separate: Must be re-runnable after any partial search without re-querying.
verdict.if_removed: Ids would change between runs and break traceability.
verdict.merge: Could live in A2.s, at the cost of per-query resume.
verdict.duplication: scholar_dedup tool overlaps conceptually; A2.m is the canonical one.
verdict.boundary: Two owned files, one shared append-only registry by part.
verdict.alternatives: Hash-based ids (rejected: order-dependent numbering is human-readable and append-only).
verdict.risks: Fuzzy-title merges may merge distinct papers (threshold 0.85 in the original engine).

units.name: Per-query check
units.necessity: Judges, per query, whether it asked well (ok / replan / accept-weak) from tool-computed signals, and routes fixes back as declared revisions.
units.trigger: After A2.m; again after each re-plan round (LOOP-01, at most two).

side_effects: declared revisions of ART-step0.strategy (query-revise, anchors) and ART-step0.frame (add/retire terms)

logic: tool computes signals per query: on-anchor share, top titles, overlap, known items found
model judges each query ok / replan / accept-weak with a reason; ambiguous terms keep / retire
a query with on-anchor share under 50% cannot be ok
replan -> query-revise / add-terms / retire-terms -> search --only -> merge -> new round (<= 2 re-plan rounds; a round adding < 5% new papers ends re-planning)
accept-weak and missing known items become must-disclose caveats
units.state: Verdicts stored per round (r0, r1, r2); signals cached per round.

error_boundary.local_recovery: LOOP-01 bounded by 2 re-plan rounds and saturation

units.idempotency: Re-setting identical verdicts is a no-op; a re-plan round is a new round id.
units.security: No network itself (the re-run search is A2.s).

verdict.problem: Volume is not quality (slide 2): off-topic or zero-hit queries pass unnoticed otherwise.
verdict.why_separate: Judgement after mechanics; owns the only interface back to A1 (LOOP-01).
verdict.if_removed: Bad queries would flow into a costly screening.
verdict.merge: Merging into A3 would mix query-level and paper-level judgement.
verdict.boundary: Owns its verdict file; revisions to A1 go through declared tools only.
verdict.cost_risk: Small token cost; each re-plan round re-queries the network.
verdict.quality: Signals computed by tool; stale verdicts detected (R-codes); L4.
verdict.alternatives: Fixed query sets without feedback (original engine).
verdict.evidence: slide 3 A2.c; run 2026-10-17 kept the Q3 ambiguous term after review.
verdict.benefits: Search quality is measured per query and repaired within a bound.
verdict.risks: Model may approve weak queries; on-anchor 50% floor limits this.

units.name: Bibliometrics
units.necessity: Computes the impact axis (normalised citation percentile, in-collection citations, SNIP) by rule, so it is never judged.
units.trigger: GATE-a2-check passed; again after A5 additions (LOOP-04).

side_effects: OpenAlex works/sources, Scopus SNIP/SJR, S2 abstract fill (recorded)

logic: fetch type, retraction, language, citations, venue per candidate
impact = 1 + 4 x (0.7 field-normalised citation percentile + 0.3 in-collection percentile), venue prior for papers under 2 years
fill missing abstracts from OpenAlex then Semantic Scholar

error_boundary.local_recovery: no OpenAlex record -> neutral impact 3.0 (no-metadata); no SNIP (snip-unavailable); abstracts partially filled (abstract-fill-partial)
error_boundary.escalation: hard stop without a candidate collection

units.security: Outbound to OpenAlex, Scopus (key), Semantic Scholar.

verdict.problem: Model-judged impact is biased and irreproducible.
verdict.why_separate: Network fetch of metadata is separate from both exclusion rules (A3.g) and judgement (A3).
verdict.if_removed: A3 would need venue/citation info, which its scorers must not see.
verdict.merge: Could merge with A3.g; kept apart because A3.g is pure and cheap to re-run.
verdict.evidence: slide 3 A3.b 'impact 用算的，不用判的'.
verdict.risks: Field normalisation depends on OpenAlex concepts.

units.name: Mechanical gate
units.necessity: Excludes retractions, non-research items and out-of-language papers before any scoring, by rule.
logic: X-RET retracted
X-TYPE not a research report (editorial, erratum, letter, ...)
X-LANG not in the protocol's languages (an English abstract passes)
missing type or language -> pass (recall first)

error_boundary.local_recovery: metadata gaps pass the paper on (degraded by design)

failure_modes: step3_bibliometrics.json missing or unreadable (hard stop: A3.b not done)
a work type or language the rule table does not know (passed through: recall first)
a retraction the metadata does not flag (not excluded here; A3's scorers may still exclude it)

verdict.problem: Scoring retracted or non-research items wastes tokens and contaminates the shortlist.
verdict.why_separate: Pure, instant, re-runnable; its codes are mechanical and auditable.
verdict.if_removed: Scorers would see items that are excluded by rule anyway.
verdict.merge: Possible with A3.b; separation keeps a pure step apart from a networked one.

units.name: Scoring and shortlist
units.necessity: Decides per paper whether it belongs, evidence first: scorers quote verbatim before scoring and never see venue or citations; the build computes composite, tiers and roles.
units.trigger: After A3.g; again incrementally for A5 additions (LOOP-04).

context: bibliometrics are used only at build, never shown to scorers

side_effects: criteria amendments recorded beside the protocol (LOOP-03)

preconditions: no open human override without a reason
logic: plan batches of 60 papers (bulk rule: relevance <= 2 only for papers with no anchor term and sem_pct < 25)
fan out one subagent per batch: quote evidence, then score relevance and quality 1-5, exclusions name a criterion
merge answers; an unqualified single entry is returned for re-scoring
build: composite = 0.50 relevance + 0.30 quality + 0.20 impact; include at >= 3.00; tiers; roles (foundational, core method, frontier, review)
apply _human overrides (include/exclude/reread) and record them apart
units.state: Per collection, incremental batches; build refuses to write anything when a check fails.

error_boundary.local_recovery: batch without answer re-dispatched; invalid item re-scored; no SPECTER2 -> no novelty signal
error_boundary.escalation: few-included (< 10 papers) is a must-disclose caveat; any build check failure stops (nothing written)

units.idempotency: Merge is keyed by paper id and batch; build is deterministic from the merged scores.
units.security: Subagents see only their batch file (titles/abstracts); no network; no venue/citation information (blinding).
units.performance: Run 2026-10-17: 20 subagents, 1.83 M tokens, 1,050 candidates -> 300 included.

verdict.problem: Inclusion decisions must be traceable to quoted evidence and blind to prestige.
verdict.why_separate: The only paper-level judgement; fan-out isolates batches; the build is the only writer of the shortlist.
verdict.merge: Plan/score/merge/build are substeps, not Units: one owner of the inclusion decision.
verdict.boundary: Owns three files; shortlist shared by part with A4.k and A6.c.
verdict.cost_risk: The most expensive Stage A search step (1.83 M tokens in the reference run).
verdict.alternatives: Single-call scoring (original engine) - no evidence quotes, no blinding.
verdict.risks: Token cost scales with the collection; scorer drift across batches.

units.name: Snowball
units.necessity: Fills the keyword search's blind spots along the citation graph; every addition is screened again by A3.
units.trigger: GATE-a3-check passed; a second round only when round 1 grew the included set by >= 10% (LOOP-04).

side_effects: OpenAlex cites:/works and S2 recommendation calls (recorded)

logic: backward: works cited by >= max(3, 2% of included) included papers, cap 40
co-citation: among papers citing >= 2 seeds, works they cite >= max(3, 2%) times, own pool, cap 20
forward: papers citing >= 2 seeds (10 seeds), cap 40
similar: S2 recommendations for 10 seeds, cap 30
additions go back to A3.b -> A3.g -> A3 with relevance >= 3
units.state: Per collection and round; seeds and thresholds recorded per round; a person's seed override redoes the round.

error_boundary.local_recovery: no OpenAlex references -> S2 fallback (backward-fallback); refs-sparse; similar-skipped; no metadata excluded
error_boundary.escalation: neither backward nor forward ran -> snowball-failed (must disclose); round 2 without 10% growth is refused

units.idempotency: Round identity + recorded answers; replay reproduces additions.
units.security: Outbound to OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar.

verdict.problem: Classic papers everyone cites are missed by keyword search (FASTER was recovered by backward search, cited by 52 included papers).
verdict.why_separate: Own network routes and thresholds; feeds A3 through a declared loop.
verdict.if_removed: Recall drops; the 2026-10-17 run added 117 papers.
verdict.merge: The four routes stay one Unit (D-05); errors carry the route as instance.
verdict.boundary: One owned file plus its part of the id registry.
verdict.dependencies: A3; the loop back to A3 is declared.
verdict.alternatives: Snowball before screening (slide 2 order) - seeds would be unscreened.
verdict.risks: Toolbox papers everyone cites (mitigated by relevance >= 3).

units.name: Citation keys
units.necessity: Gives every shortlisted paper one key for good; the key names every PDF, full text and citation after it.
preconditions: A3 done on the final shortlist
A5 done, or --no-snowball with a reason (caveat exported-before-snowball, must disclose)
logic: mint from the most complete author list
a collision takes the next unused suffix
a key that left the shortlist is retired and never handed out again
project keys into the shortlist
units.state: Append-only key log; projection into the shortlist is recomputed.

error_boundary.escalation: hard stop when A3 is not done, or A5 is not done without a reason

units.idempotency: Re-running on the same shortlist mints nothing new; keys are never renamed.

verdict.problem: Keys used as file names must never change (slide 2 trap: export in the wrong order).
verdict.why_separate: A one-way, append-only naming decision with no network dependence.
verdict.if_removed: File names and citations would break when the shortlist changes.
verdict.merge: With A4.b would make key minting depend on Crossref availability.
verdict.alternatives: Keys at export before snowball (slide 2) - rejected (D-14).

units.name: BibTeX
units.necessity: Writes one complete BibTeX entry per active key from Crossref by DOI, falling back to the search record.

side_effects: Crossref requests (40 DOIs per request, recorded under _state/net/http/)

logic: batch DOIs to Crossref
fill type, authors, venue, volume, issue, pages
papers Crossref does not know keep the search-record entry
--offline builds everything from search records (caveat bib-offline)

error_boundary.local_recovery: Crossref batch failure keeps the search-record entry
error_boundary.escalation: hard stop when A4.k is not done

verdict.problem: Writeup needs complete, correct bibliographic entries.
verdict.why_separate: Network-dependent enrichment separate from key minting.
verdict.if_removed: Writeup would build references from partial search records.

substeps.name: Plan batches
substeps.purpose: Split the candidates into blinded batch files of 60 papers and apply the bulk rule.
substeps.error_boundary: RP-NONE: a plan error stops the Unit.

substeps.name: Score in parallel (fan-out)
substeps.purpose: One subagent per batch quotes evidence, then scores relevance and quality; exclusions name the criterion.
substeps.error_boundary: RP-FANOUT-BATCH: a missing or invalid batch answer is re-dispatched once; batches are independent (failure isolation).

substeps.name: Merge answers
substeps.purpose: Validate and merge batch answers into screening_scores.json; return unqualified single entries for re-scoring.
substeps.error_boundary: Invalid entries are rejected item by item (fan-in never accepts a partial entry).

substeps.name: Build the shortlist
substeps.purpose: Compute composite, inclusion, tiers and roles; apply human overrides; write the shortlist only when every check passes.
substeps.error_boundary: All-or-nothing: any failing check writes nothing.

substeps.name: Backward
substeps.purpose: Works cited by >= max(3, 2% of the included papers); cap 40.
substeps.error_boundary: No OpenAlex references -> Semantic Scholar fallback (backward-fallback).

substeps.name: Co-citation
substeps.purpose: Count only papers citing >= 2 seeds; works they cite >= max(3, 2%) times; a pool of its own; cap 20.

substeps.name: Forward
substeps.purpose: OpenAlex cites: papers citing >= 2 seeds; seeds re-chosen when their screening changes.
substeps.error_boundary: Backward and forward both failing -> snowball-failed (must disclose).

substeps.name: Semantic neighbours
substeps.purpose: Semantic Scholar recommendations for up to 10 seeds; cap 30.
substeps.error_boundary: 429 -> one retry after 120 s; else similar-skipped.
